name: direct non-UTF8 Git blob publication and readback probe

verification.raw_utf8_fetch_control: fetching the blob through a UTF-8-only blob reader raised UnicodeDecodeError at byte 0xff position 1, consistent with the stored object being actual non-UTF8 bytes rather than base64 text
verification.duplicate_create_blob: same base64 payload returned the same blob SHA 7238568a760f480ecee2880a9ad2c21c362a1429
verification.duplicate_retry_decision: DONE_NOOP once branch/path readback already names expected blob

design_revision.before: Binary-semantic preservation was limited to canonical base64 text; actual binary byte materialization was considered unresolved without LFS/artifact storage or an external executor.
design_revision.after: The current scheduled-Chat GitHub connector exposes Git create_blob with encoding=base64 plus tree/commit/ref APIs. A bounded actual non-UTF8 file can therefore be created and read back on an isolated role-local branch with ordinary Git objects, zero optional monthly quota and no hosted executor. The unresolved boundary moves to consuming/submitting those bytes through separate unavailable APIs or execution environments.

scope_limits: Probe is nine bytes on one isolated unprotected evidence branch; bounded protocol caps payload at 64 KiB and 16 files pending larger-scale tests.
No protected or primary branch was updated by the binary publication protocol.
Does not solve arbitrary compile/test/dependency execution or downstream opaque binary-upload APIs.
Normal Git repository health/storage limits still exist; this is not a large-binary service and deliberately avoids LFS.
